defects.classification: required omission and supported preservation loss
defects.finding: The final allows a documented weaker metadata policy for mutable linked files while retaining the never-stale current-preview invariant. It does not require that the keyed revision/digest describes the bytes the handler consumed. A read-only capability is not an immutable snapshot. The discovery explicitly proposed rendering an immutable local snapshot and checking currentness; the final reduces that safeguard to an owner cost choice.
defects.consequence: An external file can change during parsing and return to its initial content before pre-publication checks. Pre/post digests can match while the rendered bytes depict the intermediate revision; coarse metadata is weaker still. A successful result can then be accepted under the wrong revision. This is a planning-contract counterexample, not an executed product failure.
defects.counterevidence_considered: Immutable app-owned input, strong trustworthy library revisions, generation gates and metadata collision warnings are present. They do not close the explicitly allowed mutable/weaker-policy branch. Unknown library semantics and snapshot cost may remain open, but cannot weaken the required display invariant.
